rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers polytheists astonished by one God and demanding a sign: created phenomena provide the proof they requested.
rows.anchor: ولما عجب المشركون من إله واحد وطلبوا آية على ذلك نزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day differ in color, length, and shortness, and alternate in departing and returning.
rows.anchor: فى اللون والطول والقصر وتعاقبهما فى الذهاب والمجئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ships carry what benefits people, or benefit people through what they transport.
rows.anchor: مما يحمل فيها أو بنفع الناس ومن فى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain descends from the sky, revives the earth after its dryness, and God disperses every creeping creature through it.
rows.anchor: ثم عطف على أنزل ﴿ فأحيا به ﴾ بالماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word min marks origin with sky and species with water; it may also be partitive because rain is the first portion of what descends.
rows.anchor: لابتداء الغاية وفى ﴿ من ماء ﴾ مطر ومن لبيان الجنس

rows.speaker: حمزة وعلى
rows.claim: They read الريح in the singular; winds turn among directions and conditions, including hot, cold, stormy, gentle, barren, pollinating, merciful, and punitive.
rows.anchor: الريح حمزة وعلى أى وتقليبها فى مهابها قبولا ودبورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clouds are subdued to God's will and rain wherever He wishes; rational reflection infers the Creator's power, wisdom, and oneness.
rows.anchor: المذلل المنقاد لمشيئة الله تعالى فيمطر حيث شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report warns of woe for reciting this verse without reflection or taking heed.
rows.anchor: وفى الحديث ويل لمن قرأ هذه الآية فمج بها أى لم يتفكر فيها ولم يعتبر بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the concession, after evening prayer or sleep a fasting man could no longer eat, drink, or have intercourse until the next night.
rows.anchor: كان الرجل إذا أمسى حل له الأكل والشرب والجماع إلى أن يصلى العشاء الاخرة

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: After intercourse with his wife following the late prayer, Umar wept, reproached himself, and told the Prophet; the concession was revealed.
rows.anchor: إن عمر رضى الله عنه واقع أهله بعد صلاة العشاء الاخرة فلما اغتسل أخذ يبكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رفث means intercourse; إلى takes the verb because it includes the sense of ifḍāʾ, and the euphemism reflects disapproval of what occurred before permission.
rows.anchor: استقباحا لما وجد منهم قبل الاباحة كما سماه اختيانا لأنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spouses are garments because they embrace and envelop each other; alternatively, each protects the other from the forbidden.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الرجل والمرأة يعتنقان ويشتمل كل واحد منهما على صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garment image explains the concession: intimate contact makes abstinence difficult, so intercourse was permitted at night.
rows.anchor: قل صبركم عنهن وصعب عليكم اجتنابهن فلذا رخص لكم فى مباشرتهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They wronged themselves through intercourse, losing a share of good; ikhtiyān intensifies khiyāna, as iktisāb intensifies kasb.
rows.anchor: تظلمونها بالجماع وتنقصونها حظها من الخير والاختيان من الخيانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepted their repentance when they repented of the prohibited act and pardoned what they had done before the concession.
rows.anchor: حين تبتم مما ارتكبتم من المحظور ﴿ وعفا عنكم ﴾ ما فعلتم قبل الرخصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Now directly means have intercourse during fasting nights; mubāshara is named for the spouses' skin touching.
rows.anchor: جامعوهن فى ليالى الصوم وهو أمر إباحة وسميت المجامعه مباشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما كتب الله لكم means seek the offspring assigned and recorded by God through intercourse, rather than satisfying desire alone; alternatively seek the lawful partner, not the forbidden.
rows.anchor: واطلبوا ما قسم الله لكم وأثبت فى اللوح من الولد بالمباشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The white thread is the first horizontal dawn light; the black thread is the stretched darkness of night.
rows.anchor: هو أول ما يبدو من الفجر المعترض فى الأفق كالخيط الممدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min of dawn identifies the white thread as dawn, implicitly clarifying the black one too; it may mean part of dawn, its beginning.
rows.anchor: بيان أن الخيط الأبيض من الفجر لا من غيره واكتفى به عن بيان الخيط الأسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding min of dawn turns the metaphor into an explicit, eloquent comparison, as saying 'a lion of so-and-so' makes the intended comparison clear.
rows.anchor: أخرجه من باب الاستعارة وصيره تشبيها بليغا

rows.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
rows.claim: He put a white and black cord under his pillow and could not distinguish them; the Prophet explained that the phrase means daylight and night darkness.
rows.anchor: عن عدى بن حاتم قال عمدت إلى عقالين أبيض وأسود فجعلتهما تحت وسادتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports daytime intention for Ramadan fasting, delaying ritual washing until dawn, forbidding continuous fasting, requiring expiation for eating or drinking, and not invalidating fasting through major ritual impurity.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على جدواز النية بالنهار فى صوم رمضان وعلى جواز تأخير الغسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercourse is lawful on Ramadan nights only for someone not in retreat; the circumstantial clause also shows retreat is only in a mosque, with no mosque-specific restriction.
rows.anchor: بين أن الجماع يحل فى ليالى رمضان لكن لغير المعتكف والجملة فى موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stated limits are God's defined rulings; do not approach them through violation or alteration, so that people may avoid prohibitions.
rows.anchor: ﴿ تلك ﴾ الأحكام التى ذكرت ﴿ حدود الله ﴾ أحكامه المحدودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening 'or like the one' has an omitted 'Have you seen?' supplied by the earlier question; both expressions signal wonder, or the syntax follows meaning rather than wording.
rows.anchor: معناه أو أرأيت مثل الذى فحذف لدلالة ألم تر عليه

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf's author says the kāf is redundant and alladhī coordinates with the person who disputed Abraham.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب الكشف فيه الكاف زائدة والذى عطف على قوله إلى الذى حاج

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan identifies the passerby as an unbeliever in resurrection, linked with Nimrod by context and by the expression of incredulity.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن أن المار كان كافرا بالبعث لا نتظامه مع نمرود

rows.speaker: الأكثر
rows.claim: Most identify the passerby as Ezra, who sought to witness revival and increase certainty, as Abraham had; his question admits ignorance of how and magnifies God's power.
rows.anchor: والأكثر أنه عزيز أراد أن يعاين إحياء الموتى ليزداد بصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruined town is Jerusalem, destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar; it is also the town from which thousands had departed.
rows.anchor: هى بيت المقدس حيث خربه بختنصر وهى التى خرج منها الألوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The roofs may have fallen together with their supports, or roofs fell first and walls then collapsed on them.
rows.anchor: مع سفوفها أو سقطت السقوف ثم سقطت عليها الحيطان كل مر عرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks how God will revive the town's inhabitants after their death; God then caused the passerby to die for a hundred years and raised him.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قال أنى يحيي ﴾ أى كيف ﴿ هذه ﴾ أى أهل هذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His estimate of a day or part of one was conjecture; he died in the morning and awoke before sunset a century later, so he first saw a day then the remaining sun.
rows.anchor: بناء على الظن وفيه دليل جواز الاجتهاد روى أنه مات ضحى وبعث بعد مائة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His food was figs and grapes and his drink juice and milk; the fruit seemed freshly picked and the drink unchanged.
rows.anchor: روى أن طعامه كان تينا وعنبا وشرابه عصيرا ولبنا فوجد التين والعنب كما جنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لم يتسنه means it did not change; its final h may be radical or a pause h, deriving from سنة as سنهة or سنوة; Hamza and Kisāʾī omit h in connected reading but retain it at pause.
rows.anchor: لم يتغير والهاء أصليه أو هاء سكت واشتقاقه من السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His donkey's bones had separated and decayed; alternatively, the donkey remained alive where tied for a hundred years without food or water, a great sign.
rows.anchor: كيف تفرقت عظامه ونخرت وكان له حمار قد ربطه فمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ezra's return was a sign: one account says he arrived mounted and recited the Torah from memory after no one had recited it visibly before him; another says his children were old while he was young.
rows.anchor: وقيل رجع إلى منزله فرأى أولاده شيوخا وهو شاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bones are either the donkey's or the bones of the dead whose revival he questioned; nunsizuhā means move and raise them together, while Hijazi and Basran read nunshiruhā, 'revive them.'
rows.anchor: أى عظام الحمار أو عظام الموتى الذين تعجب من إحيائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clothing bones with flesh is a metaphor; in 'when it became clear to him' the understood complement is that God can do all things, or what had puzzled him: resurrection.
rows.anchor: جعل اللحم كاللباس مجازا ﴿ فلما تبين له ﴾ فاعله مضمر تقديره

rows.speaker: حمزة وعلى
rows.claim: They read aʿlam as an imperative: God tells Ezra to know, or Ezra addresses himself; the other reading is his statement that he knows.
rows.anchor: قال أعلم على لفظ الامر حمزة وعلى أى قال الله له اعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After demonstrating God's power to revive, the passage urges spending in God's path and promises a great reward that He is able to grant.
rows.anchor: ولما برهن على قدرته على الإحياء حث على الإنفاق فى سبيل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison omits a possessive: it means the likeness of their expenditure, or the likeness of a sower who plants a seed.
rows.anchor: لا بد من حذف مضاف أى مثل نفقتهم ﴿ كمثل حبة ﴾ أو مثلهم كمثل باذر حبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the true grower, but the seed is credited with growing because it is the cause; one stem branches into seven ears of a hundred grains each.
rows.anchor: المنبت هو الله ولكن الحبة لما كانت سببا أسند إليها الإنبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image makes multiplied rewards visible; millet and sorghum exemplify it, and wheat can sometimes branch to this yield in fertile soil; the parable also works hypothetically.
rows.anchor: وهذا التمثيل تصوير للأضعاف كأنها ماثلة بين عينى الناظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sanābil replaces the expected plural sunbulāt just as qurūʾ replaces aqrāʾ.
rows.anchor: ووضع سنابل موضع سنبلات كوضع قروء موضع أقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not multiply seven hundredfold for every spender because conditions differ, or He may increase beyond seven hundred for whom He wills.
rows.anchor: لا لكل منفق لتفاوت أحوال المنفقين أو يزيد على سبعمائة لمن يشاء

rows.speaker: الشامي
rows.claim: The Shami reading has yudaʿʿifu; the Makki reading has yuḍāʿifu.
rows.anchor: لتفاوت أحوال المنفقين أو يزيد على سبعمائة لمن يشاء يضعف شامى ويضعف مكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is abundant in grace and generosity and knows spenders' intentions.
rows.anchor: واسع الفضل والجود ﴿ عليم ﴾ بنيات المنفقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mann is reminding a recipient of one's favor and treating it as a debt owed; people were told to forget their good deeds after doing them.
rows.anchor: هو أن يعتد على من أحسن إليه بإحسانه ويريه أنه اصطنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adhā is acting superior to the recipient because of the gift.
rows.anchor: هو أن يتطاول عليه بسبب ما أعطاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then marks the moral contrast: avoiding reproach and hurt is better than the act of giving, as steadfast faith is better than entering faith.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ثم إظهار التفاوت بين الانفاق وترك المن والأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reward is their spending's recompense; they need not fear its reduction or punishment and need not grieve lost reward.
rows.anchor: أى ثواب انفاقهم ﴿ ولا خوف عليهم ﴾ من بخس الأجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse says 'their reward' without fa because its relative clause is not conditional; the later verse includes the conditional sense.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال هنا لهم أجرهم وفيما بعد فلهم أجرهم لأن الموصول هنا لم يضمن معنى الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison to steadfastness after entering faith is phrased as a link to the verse 'then they remained steadfast.'
rows.anchor: كما جعل الاستقامة على الإيمان خيرا من الدخول فيه بقوله ثم استقاموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A courteous reply and forgiveness of a petitioner, if the request burdens the person asked, are better than charity followed by hurt; alternatively, the reply earns God's forgiveness.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قول معروف ﴾ رد جميل ﴿ ومغفرة ﴾ وعفو عن السائل إذا وجد منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite subject can validly take the predicate خير because it is qualified by a description.
rows.anchor: وصح الاخبار على المبتدأ الكرة لاختصاصه بالصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has no need of a donor who reproaches or hurts the recipient; His forbearance delays punishment, which is a warning.
rows.anchor: لا حاجة له إلى منفق يمن ويؤذى ﴿ حليم ﴾ عن معاجلته بالعقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf grammatically describes an omitted verbal noun: do not nullify charity with invalidation like that of the hypocrite who gives for display and lacks faith in God and the Last Day.
rows.anchor: الكاف نصب صفة مصدر محذوف والتقدير بطلا مثل ابطال الذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The smooth rock covered with dust represents a hypocrite's useless spending; a downpour strips it bare, leaving no reward for what was earned.
rows.anchor: مثله ونفقته التى لا ينتفع بها ألبته بحجر أملس عليه تراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular relative can denote a class or group, explaining why the text shifts to plural 'they cannot'; alternatively the kāf is circumstantial.
rows.anchor: أراد بالذى ينفق الجنس أو الفريق الذى ينفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not guide people who choose disbelief for as long as they remain committed to it.
rows.anchor: ماداموا مختارين الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's approval and تثبيت mean affirming Islam and truly believing in recompense from within oneself; spending evidences sincere faith in reward.
rows.anchor: أى وتصديقا للاسلام وتحقيقا للجزاء من أصل أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min marks the origin of تثبيت, coordinated with the purpose of spending; the likeness concerns the standing of their purified expenditure with God.
rows.anchor: ومن لابتداء الغاية وهو معطوف على المفعول له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A garden on high ground is especially apt because its trees produce purer and better fruit.
rows.anchor: وخصها لأن الشجر فيها أزكى وأحسن ثمرا

rows.speaker: عاصم والشامي
rows.claim: They read the word for high ground as rabwa.
rows.anchor: بربوة عاصم وشامى

rows.speaker: نافع ومكي وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Their reading gives the word for its produce the vocalization recorded in the source.
rows.anchor: ثمرتها أكلها نافع ومكى و أبو عمرو ﴿ ضعفين ﴾ مثلى ما كانت تثمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A downpour makes the garden yield twice its previous crop; even a light drizzle suffices because of the excellence of its soil.
rows.anchor: مثلى ما كانت تثمر قبل بسبب الوابل ﴿ فإن لم يصبها وابل فطل ﴾ فمطر صغير القطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden and its rains portray the spenders' large or small expenditures: either is pure and increases their nearness and good standing with God when done for His approval.
rows.anchor: وكما أن كل واحد من المطرين يضعف أكل الجنة فكذلك نفقتهم كثيرة كانت أو قليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees both the amount spent and the intentions behind it, including any ostentation.
rows.anchor: يرى أعمالكم على إكثار وإقلال ويعلم نياتكم فيهما من رياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza expresses denial of the prospect of such a loss.
rows.anchor: فى ﴿ أيود أحدكم ﴾ للانكار أن تكون له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden is described with dates and grapes because they are the noblest, most beneficial trees; all fruits are then added by generalization.
rows.anchor: لما كانا أكرم الشجر وأكثرها منافع خصهما بالذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction before old age is circumstantial, as is the clause about weak offspring; the garden is the aged owner's livelihood and theirs.
rows.anchor: أولاد صغار للحال أيضا والجملة فى موضع الحال من الهاء فى أصابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An iʿṣār is a whirlwind that rotates over the ground and rises skyward like a column; fire is raised by the ظرف because the ظرف functions as an adjective of the whirlwind.
rows.anchor: ريح تستدير فى الأرض ثم تسطع نحوالسماء كالعمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden's destruction depicts ostentatious good deeds found null at resurrection, causing the anguish of an elderly person whose weak children depend on the ruined garden.
rows.anchor: فيتحسر عند ذلك حسرة من كانت له جنة جامعة للثمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As with the preceding explanation of monotheism and religion, the signs are clarified to prompt reflection and awaken people.
rows.anchor: كهذا البيان الذى بين فيما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spend from good-quality earnings; this supports the obligation of zakat on trade goods.
rows.anchor: من جياد مكسوباتكم وفيه دليل وجوب الزكاة فى أموال التجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God brings from earth includes grain, fruit, and minerals; 'good things' is omitted because the preceding phrase already supplies it.
rows.anchor: من الحب والثمر والمعادن وغيرها والتقدير ومن طيبات ما أخرجنا لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not deliberately choose inferior property to give; the phrase is circumstantial, describing one who intends to make that the expenditure.
rows.anchor: ولا تقصدوا المال الردئ ﴿ منه تنفقون ﴾ تخصونه بالانفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: You would accept such property for your own dues only by tolerating a concession; the idiom for overlooking one's right is likened to closing one's eyes.
rows.anchor: إلا بأن تتسامحوا فى أخذه وتترخصوا فيه من قولك أعمض فلان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: People used to give poor dates and the worst dates as charity, and were forbidden to do so.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما كانوا يتصدقون بحشف التمر وشراره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is independent of people's charity and worthy of praise.
rows.anchor: ﴿ واعلموا أن الله غني ﴾ عن صدقاتكم ﴿ حميد ﴾ مستحق للحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan promises that spending will make people poor; the word promise can refer to either good or evil.
rows.anchor: فى الانفاق ﴿ الفقر ﴾ ويقول لكم إن عاقبة إنفاقكم أن تفقروا والوعد يستعمل فى الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's command to indecency means inciting miserliness and withholding charity; Arabs call a miser fāḥish.
rows.anchor: ويغريكم على البخل ومنع الصدقات واغراء الآمر للمأمور والفاحش عند العرب البخيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises forgiveness and expiation for sins, plus either better replacement for what was spent or reward in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: و أن يخلف عليكم أفضل مما انفقتم أو ثوابا عليه فى الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants expansively to whom He wills and knows people's actions and intentions.
rows.anchor: يوسع على من يشاء ﴿ عليم ﴾ بأفعالكم ونياتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly spending may be for prestige, generosity, and good reputation, or an attempt to draw near to God while remaining unbelievers.
rows.anchor: فى المفاخر والمكارم وكسب الثناء وحسن الذكر بين الناس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ṣirr in the wind means severe cold.
rows.anchor: برد شديد عن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind-and-field image can mean a destructive wind consuming the crop, or the destruction of their spending as a wind destroys a crop; ṣirr is parsed as a genitive description of wind.
rows.anchor: كمثل مهلك ربح وهو الحرث أو مثل اهلاك ما ينفقون كمثل اهلاك ريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crop owners wronged themselves through disbelief, so its destruction is punishment; God did not wrong them.
rows.anchor: عقوبة على كفرهم ﴿ وما ظلمهم الله ﴾ باهلاك حرثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronouns refer to the spenders: God did not wrong them by rejecting their expenditure; they wrong themselves by failing to provide a basis for acceptance.
rows.anchor: أو يكون الضمير للمنفقين أى وما ظلمهم الله بأن لم يقبل نفقاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The t- and y-readings allow different implied subjects: on one parse bukhul is supplied, هو is a separator, and خير is the second object; with the y-reading the subject may be the Prophet or another person.
rows.anchor: من قرأ بالتاء قدر مضافا محذوفا أى ولا تحسبن بخل الباخلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the hoarders themselves are subject, the understood phrase is 'their miserliness'; هو remains a separator and خير the second object.
rows.anchor: ومن جعل فاعله الذين يبخلون كان التقدير ولا يحسبن الذين يبخلون بخلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miserliness is evil because wealth will leave them while its burden remains with them.
rows.anchor: أى البخل ﴿ شر لهم ﴾ لأن اموالهم ستزول عنهم ويبقى عليهم وبال البخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says a person withholding zakat will have the wealth made into a male bald snake with two fangs, placed around his neck to bite and drive him toward the Fire.
rows.anchor: كما جاء فى الحديث من منع زكاة ماله يصير حية ذكرا اقرع له نابان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inherits everything in the heavens and earth; the hoarders withhold what belongs to Him. Mawārith derives from mawārith with wāw changed to yāʾ after kasra.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولله ميراث السماوات والأرض ﴾ وله مافيهما مما يتوارثه أهلهما من مال وغيره

rows.speaker: المكي وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They read the closing verb with yāʾ; the t-reading is a rhetorical shift that intensifies the threat, while yāʾ follows the apparent subject.
rows.anchor: فالتاء على طريقة الالتفات وهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation and alternation are clear proofs of an eternal, knowing, wise, powerful Maker for people whose reason is free of desire, like a kernel freed from husk.
rows.anchor: لأدلة واضحة على صانع قديم عليم حكيم قادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A substance cannot be free of a newly arising accident; what cannot be free of the originated is itself originated, so it requires an eternal originator rather than an infinite regress.
rows.anchor: لأن جوهرا ما لا ينفك عن عرض حادث وما لا يخلو عن الحادث فهو حادث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beauty and precision of creation demonstrate knowledge and wisdom; its continuance demonstrates power.
rows.anchor: وحسن صنعه يدل على علمه واتقانه يدل على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report warns of woe for someone who recites this verse without reflecting on it.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام ويل لمن قرأها ولم يتفكر فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An Israelite worshipper received a cloud's shade after thirty years, but a young worshipper did not; his mother suggested he had failed to contemplate the sky, and he agreed.
rows.anchor: وحكى فيها أن فى بنى اسرائيل من إذا عبد الله ثلانين سنة أظلته سحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelite youth's mother says he received no shade except because he had once looked at the sky without reflecting.
rows.anchor: قالت فما أوتيت إلا من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance is not accepted once the dying person sees the causes of death and the angel of death: responsibility has ended, and the act is compelled rather than chosen.
rows.anchor: إلى أن يزول حال التكليف بحضور أسباب الموت ومعاينة ملك الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Acceptance is reward and promise, and can only apply to a voluntary act.
rows.anchor: وقبول التوبة ثواب ولا وعديه إلا مختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about those who die disbelieving coordinates grammatically with the earlier relative clause: there is no repentance for either group.
rows.anchor: فى موضع جر بالعطف على الذين يعملون السيئات

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr assigns the first verse to believers, the middle one to hypocrites, and the last to unbelievers.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير الآية الاولى فى المؤمنين والوسطى فى المنافقين والأخرى فى الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some codices write the phrase with two lām letters; the following demonstrative is a subject whose predicate is that painful punishment has been prepared.
rows.anchor: وفى بعض المصاحف بلامين وهو مبتدأ خبره ﴿ أولئك أعتدنا لهم عذابا أليما ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commanding warning of the non-pious, God commands drawing the pious near and forbids their dismissal.
rows.anchor: ولما أمر النبى عليه السلام بإنذار غير المتقين ليتقوا أمر بعد ذلك بتقريب المتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling on God morning and evening means continuous worship, or specifically dawn and afternoon prayers, or all five prayers; the Shami reading has the stated form of 'morning.'
rows.anchor: أى عبادته ويواظبون عليها والمراد بذكر الغداة والعشى الدوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's face means sincerity; 'face' can denote a thing's essence and reality.
rows.anchor: ووسمهم بالإخلاص فى عبادتهم بقوله ﴿ يريدون وجهه ﴾ فالوجه يعبر به عن ذات الشئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation followed the chiefs' demand to dismiss poor believers Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar, and others; the Prophet refused, they requested alternate days and a written agreement, then the poor moved aside as Ali was called to write. The Prophet threw away the paper and embraced them.
rows.anchor: نزلت فى الفقراء بلال وصهيب وعمار وأضرابهم حين قال رؤساء المشركين لو طردت هؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers' account is theirs alone and cannot transfer to the Prophet; the source compares the statement with a verse about Noah's reckoning.
rows.anchor: حسباهم عليهم لازم لهم لا يتعداهم اليك كما أن حسابك عليك لا يتعداك اليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The consequence clause answers the negation, while the next clause answers the prohibition; alternatively, being unjust is caused by dismissing them.
rows.anchor: جواب النفى وهو ما عليك من حسابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weighing is the weighing and distinguishing of deeds by relative heaviness; يومئذ means the day God questions nations and messengers, with the clause omitted and replaced by nunation.
rows.anchor: أي وزن الأعمال والتمييز بين راجحها وخفيفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says records of deeds will be weighed on a scale with a tongue and two pans, manifesting the attribute and ending excuses; another takes the phrase as just judgment, while God knows its manner.
rows.anchor: ثم قيل توزن صحف الأعمال يميز أن له لسان وكفتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawāzīn can mean scales or weighed deeds; what has weight and worth is good deeds or the measure used for them.
rows.anchor: جمع ميزان أو موزون أى فمن رجحت أعماله الموزونة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whose balances are heavy are the successful, meaning victorious.
rows.anchor: الفائزون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light balances belong to unbelievers: lacking faith, they have no good works that count in the scale.
rows.anchor: هم الكفار فإنه لا إيمان لهم ليعتبر معه عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They lose themselves by wronging God's signs; the signs are proofs, and wronging them means denying them and refusing to follow them.
rows.anchor: والظلم بها وضعها فى غير موضعها أي جحودها وترك الانقياد لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every nation has a fixed time for annihilating punishment if it does not believe; this threatens Mecca with a divinely known term, as earlier nations were punished.
rows.anchor: وقت معين يأتيهم فيه عذاب الاستئصال أن لم يؤمنوا وهو وعيد لأهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the term arrives it cannot be advanced or delayed; 'an hour' is used as the smallest ordinary unit of reprieve.
rows.anchor: قيد بساعة لأنها أقل ما يستعمل فى الامهال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose clause attaches to resurrection: God separates the unbelieving faction from the believing faction; Hamza and Kisāʾī have the recorded reading.
rows.anchor: واللام في ﴿ ليميز الله الخبيث ﴾ الفريق الخبيث من الكفار ﴿ من الطيب ﴾ أى من الفريق الطيب من المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God piles the wicked together, gathers them all, and casts that faction into Hell; they lose themselves and their wealth.
rows.anchor: فيحمعه ﴿ فيجعله في جهنم ﴾ أى الفريق الخبيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three left behind from the campaign were Kaʿb ibn Mālik, Murāra ibn al-Rabīʿ, and Hilāl ibn Umayya.
rows.anchor: وهم كعب بن مالك ومرارة بن الربيع وهلال بن أمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's constriction despite its breadth depicts their confusion and agitation; their hearts could hold neither comfort nor joy, and they knew no refuge from God's anger except seeking forgiveness.
rows.anchor: برحبها أى مع سعتها وهو مثل للحيرة فى أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepted their repentance after fifty days so that they could join the repentant.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ثم تاب عليهم ﴾ بعد خمسين يوما ﴿ ليتوبوا ﴾ ليكونوا من جملة التبوابين

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
rows.claim: Al-Warrāq defines sincere repentance as making earth and one's own soul feel constricted, as happened to these three.
rows.anchor: عن أبى بكر الوراق أنه قال التوبة النصوح أن تضيق على التائب الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain from clouds makes the plants of earth intertwine; these include grains, fruits, and vegetables eaten by people and grass eaten by livestock.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فاختلط به ﴾ بالماء ﴿ نبات الأرض ﴾ أى فاشتبك بسببه حتى خالط بعضه بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the earth takes on its vegetation's ornament and beautifies itself, the text personifies it like a bride wearing luxurious clothes of many colors; izzayyanat assimilates the tāʾ into zāy.
rows.anchor: وتزينت به وهو أصله وأدغمت التاء فى الزاى وهو كلام فصيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inhabitants think they control the crop and can gather its yield, but God's command strikes it by day or night and leaves it cut down as if it had never flourished; omitted possessives mean its crop.
rows.anchor: متمكنون من منفعتها محصلون لثمرتها رافعون لغلتها ﴿ أتاها أمرنا ﴾ عذابنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ams is an idiom for the recent past; the deletion in 'as if it had not flourished' supplies the crop as the subject.
rows.anchor: هو مثل فى الوقت القريب كأنه قيل كأن لم تغن آنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The compound simile portrays worldly life rapidly ending after its peak, like lush, dense vegetation drying away; it teaches that worldly pleasure is mixed with bitterness.
rows.anchor: وهذا من التشبيه المركب شبهت حال الدنيا فى سرعة تقضيها وانقراض نعيمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source quotes an unattributed line comparing life to a cup of old wine, clear at first and turbid at the end.
rows.anchor: فأوله صفو وآخره كدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An extended allegory contrasts wholesome clay yielding intimacy, piety, generosity, love, and spiritual gardens with corrupt clay producing shirk, greed, harm, and frivolity; death harvests the crop before resurrection.
rows.anchor: فالطينة الطيبة تنبت بساتين الانس ورياحين الرحوح وزهرة الزهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water benefits in small amounts and destroys in excess; worldly wealth likewise demands leaving surplus and taking provisions, while acquiring it entails missteps and hoarding destroys its owner.
rows.anchor: وكذلك حال الدنيا كالماء ينفع قليله ويهلك كثيره ولا بد من ترك مازاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is quoted saying zakat is the bridge of Islam; the allegory likens zakat to a bridge over the river of wealth, maintained by prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن هذا قال عليه السلام الزكاة قنطرة الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth favors base people rather than noble ones and gathers through a miser's toil like water collected in lowlands behind a dam; it eventually vanishes like water in the hand.
rows.anchor: وكذالك المال لا يجتمع إلا بكد البخيل كما أن الماء لا يجتمع إلا بسد المسيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection they think their worldly life or time in graves lasted only an hour; they recognize one another on emerging, then recognition ceases as the ordeal intensifies.
rows.anchor: استقصروا مدة لبثهم فى الدنيا أو فى قبورهم

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Hafs reads the verb for gathering with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وبالياء حفص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form is a shortened kāna with omitted name; recognition can be a circumstantial clause or an independent statement.
rows.anchor: ويتعارفون بينهم حال بعد حال أو مستأنف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their loss can be spoken by them or be God's testimony; they spent faith as capital and traded it for disbelief, without knowing the trade.
rows.anchor: على إرادة القول أى يتعارفون بينهم قائلين ذلك أو هي شهادة من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing statement is an independent expression of astonishment at how great their loss is.
rows.anchor: للتجارة عارفين بها وهو استئناف فيه معنى التعجب كأنه قيل ما أخسرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad cannot control harm such as illness or poverty, nor benefit such as health or wealth, except what God wills; the exception is disconnected: what God wills nevertheless occurs.
rows.anchor: استثناء منقطع أى ولكن ما شاء الله من ذلك كائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Therefore he cannot bring the audience harm or punishment by his own power.
rows.anchor: فكيف أملك لكم الضر وجلب العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every nation has a fixed, written time for punishment and cannot advance or delay it; the warning is not to demand haste.
rows.anchor: لكل أمة وقت معلوم للعذاب مكتوب فى اللوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke asks whether Pharaoh believes now, at the moment of compulsion when drowning has overtaken him and he despairs; the interrogative now is governed by 'do you believe?'
rows.anchor: أتؤمن الساعة فى وقت الاضطرار حين أدركك الغرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier disobedience made Pharaoh one of those who led others astray from faith.
rows.anchor: من الضالين المضلين عن الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel brought Pharaoh a legal question about a servant raised in his master's wealth who denied the master's favor and claimed lordship; al-Walīd ibn Muṣʿab wrote that such a rebel deserved drowning, and Gabriel showed Pharaoh the ruling as he choked.
rows.anchor: روى أن جبريل عليه السلام أتاه بفتيا ما قول الأمير فى عبد لرجل نشأ فى ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause continues the account: God destroys nations and then saves His messengers and those who believed with them.
rows.anchor: معطوف على كلام محذوف يدل عليه إلا مثل أيام الذين خلوا من قبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rescues believers among the addressed people in the same way He rescued earlier believers, while destroying the polytheists; حقا علينا is a parenthetical emphatic statement.
rows.anchor: أى مثل ذلك الانجاء ننجى المؤمنين منكم ونهلك المشركين

rows.speaker: علي وحفص
rows.claim: They read nunajji with the light form.
rows.anchor: بالتخفيف على وحفص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those seeking worldly life and its adornment receive their full wages in this world, including provision and health, without being shortchanged; they are unbelievers or hypocrites.
rows.anchor: نوصل اليهم أجور أعمالهم وافية كاملة من غير بخس فى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people receiving this worldly recompense are identified as unbelievers or hypocrites.
rows.anchor: وهو ما يرزقون فيها من الصحة الرزق وهم الكفار أو المنافقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such people have only the Fire in the afterlife; their work earns no reward there because they intended this world and received what they sought.
rows.anchor: وحبط فى الآخرة ما صنعوه أو صنيعهم أى لم يكن لهم ثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their deeds are intrinsically futile because they were done without a proper purpose; work with no valid aim merits no reward.
rows.anchor: أى كان عملهم فى نفسه باطلا لأنه لم يعلم لغرض صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The son says he will take refuge on a mountain, which he thinks will protect him from drowning.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قال سآوي ﴾ ألجأ ﴿ إلى جبل يعصمني من الماء ﴾ يمنعنى من الغرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'No protector' may mean that none can protect from God's command except God; alternatively, no refuge from the flood exists except the place where God saved the believers, the Ark.
rows.anchor: إلا الراحم وهو الله تعالى أو لا عاصم اليوم من الطوفان إلا من رحم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the exception is disconnected: the son has no refuge, but whoever God has mercy on is protected.
rows.anchor: أو هو استثناء منقطع كأنه قيل ولكن من رحمه الله فهو المعصوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wave separated either the son from the mountain or Noah from his son, and the son drowned; 'became' or 'was in God's knowledge' is possible.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وحال بينهما الموج ﴾ بين ابنه والجبل أو بين نوح وابنه ﴿ فكان من المغرقين ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disconnected-exception construction is compared with the verse saying they have no knowledge, only following conjecture.
rows.anchor: كقوله ﴿ ما لهم به من علم إلا اتباع الظن ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must remain on the commanded path without deviating; those who repent from disbelief and return sincerely to God are conjoined with him.
rows.anchor: فاستقم استقامة مثل الاستقامة التى أمرت بها غير عادل عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction with the hidden subject is allowed because of the intervening phrase; believers must not cross God's limits, since God sees and recompenses their deeds.
rows.anchor: معطوف على المستتر فى استقم وجاز للفاصل يعنى فاستقم أنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said that no verse was harder for the Prophet than this one, prompting the saying 'Hud has made me gray.'
rows.anchor: قيل ما نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم آية كان اشق عليه من هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two ends of day mean morning and evening: dawn prayer, and afternoon prayer after noon, which includes noon and afternoon; the night periods near day's end are sunset and night prayers.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار ﴾ غدوة وعشية ﴿ وزلفا من الليل ﴾ وساعات من الليل جمع زلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative dual 'ends' functions adverbially because the words are annexed to times, as in phrases giving a whole or half day.
rows.anchor: وانتصاب طرفى النهار على الظرف لانهما مضافان إلى الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The five prayers expiate sins committed between them; alternatively good deeds generally erase sins, as in the prophetic instruction to follow an evil deed with a good one.
rows.anchor: أن الصلوات الخمس يذهبن الذنوب وفى الحديث أن الصلوات الخمس تكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet also recommends saying 'Glory be to God, praise belongs to God, there is no god but God, and God is greatest.'
rows.anchor: أو سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله و الله أكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That may refer to the instruction beginning 'remain steadfast' and what follows, or to the Qur'an as admonition for those who take heed.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى فاستقم فما بعده أو القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about ʿAmr ibn Ghaziyya al-Anṣārī, a date seller who entered a woman's home and kissed her, then repented; the Prophet said his joining the afternoon prayer expiated it, and that the rule applied to everyone.
rows.anchor: نزلت فى عمرو بن غزية الأنصارى بائع التمر قال لامرأة فى البيت

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet asks whether the man prayed the afternoon prayer with them, calls it an expiation, and says this applies to all people, not him alone.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام هل شهدت معنا العصر قال نعم قال هى كفارة لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Be patient in carrying out commands and avoiding prohibitions, since none of it can be completed without patience.
rows.anchor: على امتثال ما أمرت به والانتهاء عما نهيت عنه فلا يتم شيء منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From 'remain steadfast' through 'be patient,' and other good deeds, the passage contains all commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: جاء بما هو مشتمل على جميع الاوامر والنواهى من قوله ﴿ فاستقم ﴾ إلى قوله ﴿ واصبر ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women are said to have invited Joseph because they urged him to accept their mistress and each may have privately invited him herself.
rows.anchor: اسند الدعوة عليهن لأنهن قلن له ما عليك لو أجبت مولاتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph turns to God, preferring prison to committing the sin they solicit.
rows.anchor: قال رب السجن احب إلى من ركوب المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His conditional plea asks God to turn their plot away and protect him; aṣbū means incline toward them and desire.
rows.anchor: فزع منه إلى الله فى طلب العصمة ﴿ أصب إليهن ﴾ امل اليهن والصبوة الميل إلى الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣabwa means inclination toward desire and is related to ṣabā, the pleasant breeze toward which souls incline; the ignorant are either those who fail to act on knowledge or the foolish.
rows.anchor: والصبوة الميل إلى الهوى ومنه الصبا لأن النفوس تصبوا اليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Joseph's words included a request and prayer for protection, God answered that prayer and turned the women's plot away.
rows.anchor: والدعاء قال ﴿ فاستجاب له ربه ﴾ أى أجاب الله دعاءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears the supplications of those who seek refuge and knows Joseph's condition and the women's condition.
rows.anchor: لدعوات الملتجئين إليه ﴿ العليم ﴾ بحاله وحالهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of 'it appeared to them' is implicit and supplied by the decision that they would imprison him; the pronoun refers to the minister and his household.
rows.anchor: فاعله مضمر لدلالة ما يفسره عليه وهو ليسجننه والمعنى بدا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs of Joseph's innocence included the shirt's tear, the women's cut hands, and the child's testimony.
rows.anchor: وهى الشواهد على برءاته كقد القميص وقطع الأيدى وشهادة الصبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They imprisoned him to excuse the situation and silence gossip; the minister was compliant with his wife, who hoped prison would make Joseph submit, or feared public suspicion and accepted concealment instead of separation.
rows.anchor: لإبداء عذر الحال وارخاء الستر على القيل والقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'until a time' leaves the period indefinite, as the wife apparently requested a period to see what would happen.
rows.anchor: إلى زمان كأنها اقترحت أن يسجن زمانا حتى تبصر ما يكون منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two young men were the king's enslaved baker and cupbearer, imprisoned on a poisoning accusation at the same time as Joseph; maʿa requires their entry to be in his company.
rows.anchor: عبدان للملك خبازه وشرابيه بتهمة السم فادخلا السجن ساعة ادخل يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer sees himself pressing grapes for wine; grapes are named for their outcome, or khamr is the Omani word for grapes.
rows.anchor: أى عنبا تسمية للعنب بما يؤول إليه أو الخمر بلغته عمان اسم للعنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The baker sees himself carrying bread over his head for birds to eat; they ask Joseph to interpret both dreams.
rows.anchor: فإنك تداوى المريض وتعزى الحزين وتسوع على الفقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their praise means either that Joseph interprets dreams well or that he cares for prisoners by treating the ill, comforting the sad, and helping the poor.
rows.anchor: من الذين يحسنون عبارة الرؤيا أو من المحسنين إلى أهل السجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the pair conspired to test Joseph: the cupbearer dreamed of three grape clusters from a vine and serving the king; the baker dreamed of three food baskets eaten by birds.
rows.anchor: وقيل أنهما تحالماله يمتحناه فقال الشرابى إنى رأيت كأنى فى بستان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer will return to serving his master wine and resume his former work; the baker will be crucified and birds will eat from his head.
rows.anchor: يريد الشرابى ﴿ فيسقي ربه ﴾ سيده ﴿ خمرا ﴾ أى يعود إلى عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph interprets three vine branches as three days in prison, after which the cupbearer returns to his former station; three baskets mean the baker will be killed after three days.
rows.anchor: ما رأيت من الكرمة وحسنها هو الملك وحسن حالك عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the baker denied having seen anything after hearing the interpretation, Joseph said that the matter being asked about was settled: one would perish and the other escape.
rows.anchor: أى قطع وتم ما تستفتيان فيه من أمركما وشأنكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the interpretation came through reasoning, Joseph was the one who thought the cupbearer would be saved; if by revelation, the cupbearer was the one who thought so; alternatively, ẓanna means certainty.
rows.anchor: الظان هو يوسف عليه السلام أن كان تأويله بطريق الاجتهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks the cupbearer to describe him and his case to the king in hope of release from his predicament.
rows.anchor: صفنى عند المك بصفتى وقص عليه قصتى لعله يرحمني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan made the cupbearer forget to mention Joseph to the king, or made Joseph forget God when he entrusted his affair to another.
rows.anchor: فأنسى الشرابى ﴿ ذكر ربه ﴾ أن يذكره لربه أو عند ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report says God have mercy on Joseph: had he not asked the cupbearer to remember him, he would not have remained in prison seven years; most say the years were seven, while biḍʿ means three through nine.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث رحم الله اخى يوسف لو لم يقل اذكرنى عند ربك لما لبث فى السجن سبعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Egyptian king al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid dreamed of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones and seven green ears overcome by seven dry ears; the unusual vision distressed him.
rows.anchor: رأى الملك مصر الريان بن الوليد رؤيا عجيبة هالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's ordeal began with a dream and his deliverance also came through one.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان ابتداء بلاء يوسف فى الرؤيا ثم كان سبب نجاته أيضا الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sīmān is a regular plural of fat; ʿijāf is a plural of lean, an unusual pattern for feminine afʿal adjectives, modeled on its opposite sīmān by pairing opposites.
rows.anchor: والعجاف المهازيل والعجف الهزال الذى ليس بعده سمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although only the green ears are explicitly numbered, the structure repeatedly centers on seven, so the dry ears also number seven.
rows.anchor: وفى الآية دلالة على أن سنبلات اليابسة كانت سبعا كالخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-malāʾ means the realm's prominent scholars and sages.
rows.anchor: كأنه أراد الأعيان من العلماء والحكماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in li-l-ruʾyā may clarify, reinforce a fronted object that is weaker in governing the verb, or form a predicate of kāna; taʿburūn can be another predicate or a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: اللام فى للرؤيا للبيان كقوله وكانوا فيه من الزاهدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To interpret a dream is to state its outcome, like crossing a river to its far bank; taʾwīl likewise names its end or return.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة عبرت الرؤيا ذكرت عاقبتها وأخر أمرها كما تقول عبرت النهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light form ʿabartu is the established reading; the source says scholars reject the heavy form, taʿbīr, and muʿabbir.
rows.anchor: بالتخفيف هو الذى اعتمده الإثبات ورأيتهم ينكرون عبرت بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The survivor was spared execution; after a long interval he recalled Joseph when the king's dream baffled the court and asked to be sent to him.
rows.anchor: بعد مدة طويلة وذلك أنه حين استفتى الملك فى رؤياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wād-dakara is the eloquent reading, derived from idh-takara with substitutions and assimilation; Hasan's wa-dhkur is explained as remembering Joseph and what he had witnessed.
rows.anchor: بالدال هو الفصح وأصله إذتكر فأبدلت الذال دالا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan reads wa-dhkur, meaning the survivor remembered Joseph and what he had seen; Yaʿqub reads 'send me' with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن واذكر ووجه أنه قلب التاء ذالا وأدغم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The survivor says he can report its interpretation from the person who knows it and asks to be sent to Joseph.
rows.anchor: أنا أخبركم به عمن عنده علمه ﴿ فأرسلون ﴾ وبالياء يعقوب أى فابعثونى إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement 'you will cultivate' functions as a command; following it with 'leave it in its ear' proves this. The declarative form emphasizes that the command will occur.
rows.anchor: هو خبر فى معنى الامر كقوله تؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر وتجاهدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dʾaban is read with a quiescent hamza or with it vowelled by Hafs; both are verbal nouns of diligent work and circumstantial of those addressed.
rows.anchor: يسكون الهمزة وحفص يحركه وهما مصدرا دأب فى العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leave the harvested grain in its ear so pests will not eat it, keeping only a little to eat during those years.
rows.anchor: فى سنبله كى لا يأكله السوس ﴿ إلا قليلا مما تأكلون ﴾ فى تلك السنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The famine years are said by figurative attribution to eat what their people consume from the stored harvest of the fertile years.
rows.anchor: هو من إسناد المجاز جعل اكل اهلهن مسندا إليهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stores are what the people put forward for those years, retaining only a small amount of what they protect and save.
rows.anchor: أى فى السنين المخصبة ﴿ إلا قليلا مما تحصنون ﴾ يحرزون وتخبئون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abundant year comes after the fourteen preceding years; people will receive relief, either because their pleas are answered or because it rains.
rows.anchor: أى من بعد اربع عشرة سنة عام ﴿ فيه يغاث الناس ﴾ من الغوث أى يجاب مستغيثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that year people press grapes, olives, and sesame into drinks and oils; Hamza reads the verb with the stated variant.
rows.anchor: العنب الزيتون والسمسم فيتخذون الأشربة والادهان تعصرون حمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph interprets the fat cows and green ears as plentiful years, the lean cows and dry ears as famine years, and, by revelation, announces a blessed eighth year of abundant good.
rows.anchor: فاول البقرات السمان والسنبلات الخضر بسنين مخاصيب والعجاف واليابسات بسنين مجدبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph delays answering the king's summons and asks the messenger to return and inquire about the women who cut their hands, so his innocence is public before he leaves prison.
rows.anchor: إنما تثبت يوسف وتأنى فى إجابة الملك وقدم سؤال النسوة ليظهر برءاة ساحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He wants to forestall enemies' slander and claims that his seven years in prison prove a grave crime; the episode shows that removing suspicion and avoiding accusatory situations are duties.
rows.anchor: لئلا يقولوا ما خلد فى السجن سبع سنين إلا لامر عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is quoted marveling at Joseph's patience and generosity: the source says he himself would have required release before interpreting the king's dream and would have hurried out of prison.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه السلام لقد عجبت من يوسف وكرمه وصبره والله يغفر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's gracious manners spared his former mistress: he mentions only the women who cut their hands; God knows their plot and will requite it.
rows.anchor: ومن كرمه وحسن أدبه أنه لم يذكر سيدته مع ما صنعت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king asks the women whether they felt any inclination from Joseph; their exclamation 'God forbid' expresses amazement that God created someone so chaste.
rows.anchor: هل وجدتن منه ميلا اليكن ﴿ قلن حاش لله ﴾ تعجبا من قدرته على خلق عفيف مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women deny any wrongdoing by Joseph; the minister's wife admits the truth has emerged and confirms his statement that she solicited him.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قالت امرأة العزيز الآن حصحص الحق ﴾ ظهر واستقر ﴿ أنا راودته عن نفسه وإنه لمن الصادقين ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no stronger proof of his innocence than their testimony for him and their confession against themselves; the messenger returns with their words and the wife's admission.
rows.anchor: ولا مزيد على شهادتهن له للبرءاة والنزاهة واعترافهن على انفسهن

rows.speaker: الكوفي والشامي
rows.claim: The Kufi and Shami readings use two hamzas in the question 'Are you indeed Joseph?'
rows.anchor: بهمزتين كوفي وشامي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is an initiating lām; anta is the subject and Yūsuf its predicate, and the clause is the predicate of inna.
rows.anchor: اللام لام الابتداء وأنت مبتدأ ويوسف خبره والجملة خبر ان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph mentions his brother in answering their question about his identity because it clarifies the answer.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر أخاه وهم قد سألوه عن نفسه لأنه كان في ذكر أخيه بيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He acknowledges God's favor in restoring family after separation and mentions safety and honor without reproach.
rows.anchor: بالألفة بعد الفرقة وذكر نعمة الله بالسلامة والكرامة ولم يبدأ بالملامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwā means avoiding obscenity and patience means refraining from sin and persevering in obedience; al-muḥsinīn replaces a pronoun because it encompasses both traits.
rows.anchor: عن المعاصي وعلى الطاعة ﴿ فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين ﴾ أي أجرهم فوضع المحسنين موضع الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the one who fears his Lord and patiently bears affliction will receive reward in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: وقيل من يتق مولاه ويصبر على بلواه لا يضيع أجره في دنياه وعقباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan departed from Arish in Egypt; faṣala means leaving a town and passing beyond its walls.
rows.anchor: خرجت من عريش مصر يقال فصل من البلد فصولا اذا انفصل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's scent reached Jacob by God's enabling him to smell the shirt from a journey of eight days.
rows.anchor: اوجده الله ريح القميص حين أقبل من مسيرة ثمانية أيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafnīd means attributing fand, grief, or impaired reason from old age; Jacob says they would believe him if they did not accuse him of that.
rows.anchor: التفنيد النسبة إلى الفند وهو الحزن وانكار العقل من هرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waraʾ means ahead: Hell may be described as ahead of him in this life because it awaits him as he stands on its brink, or as a description of his afterlife state.
rows.anchor: ﴿ من ورائه ﴾ من بين يديه ﴿ جهنم ﴾ وهذا وصف حاله وهو في الدنيا لأنه مرصد لجهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about being given drink coordinates with an omitted phrase about what he will encounter in Hell; ṣadīd is the pus flowing from the skin of Hell's inhabitants and clarifies the vague word water.
rows.anchor: معطوف على محذوف تقديره من ورائه جهنم يلقى فيها ما يلقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He drinks the foul liquid in successive gulps but can scarcely swallow; lā yakādu means he does not even approach swallowing, as in 'he scarcely saw it.'
rows.anchor: ﴿ يتجرعه ﴾ يشربه جرعة جرعة ﴿ ولا يكاد يسيغه ﴾ ولا يقارب أن يسيغه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death's causes come from every direction or every part of his body; the expression depicts terrible pain, each part of which would kill if death were possible.
rows.anchor: أى اسباب الموت من كل جهة أو من كل مكان من جسده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is not dead because death would bring relief; every future moment brings a punishment heavier than the last.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وما هو بميت ﴾ لأنه لو مات لاستراح ﴿ ومن ورائه ﴾ ومن بين يديه ﴿ عذاب غليظ ﴾

rows.speaker: الفضيل
rows.claim: Al-Fuḍayl says the severe punishment is cutting off the breaths and holding them in the bodies.
rows.anchor: وعن الفضيل هو قطع الانفاس وحبسها في الاجساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening likeness has an omitted predicate, 'the likeness of those who disbelieved'; likeness here is a metaphor for an extraordinary quality.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ محذوف الخبر اي فيما يتلى عليكم مثل الذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their good deeds, including kinship, freeing slaves, ransoming captives, and hosting guests, are ashes blown away because they rest on no foundation of faith.
rows.anchor: وأعمال الكفرة المكارم التي كانت لهم من صله الأرحام وعتق الرقاب

rows.speaker: المدني
rows.claim: The Madinan reading has the plural 'winds' where the other reading has 'wind.'
rows.anchor: الرياح مدنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ash image means they will find no trace or reward from their deeds, just as scattered ash cannot be recovered.
rows.anchor: لا يقدر من الرماد المطير في الريح على شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final phrase points to how far their error is from the right path or from reward.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى بعد ضلالهم عن طريق الحق أو عن الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoing means disbelief and sins; if God punished people immediately, not one creature would remain on earth.
rows.anchor: بكفرهم ومعاصيهم ﴿ ما ترك عليها ﴾ على الأرض ﴿ من دابة ﴾

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says even the bustard dies in its nest because of the wrongdoer's injustice.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن الحبارى لتموت في وكرها بظلم الظالم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the dung beetle nearly perishes in its hole because of a descendant of Adam's sin.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه كاد الجعل يهلك في جحره بذنب ابن آدم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets every creature as every moving polytheist.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما من دابة من مشرك يدب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed term may be each person's lifespan, a time set by wisdom, or the Resurrection; when it arrives, no delay or advancement is possible.
rows.anchor: أي أجل كل أحد أو وقت تقضيه الحكمة أو القيامة

rows.speaker: نافع والشامي وأبو بكر
rows.claim: These readers vocalize the initial nūn with fatḥa in the verb 'We give you drink.'
rows.anchor: وبفتح النون نافع وشامى وأبو بكر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says saqaytu and asqaytu have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج سقيته واسقيته بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anʿām is a singular-form noun on the pattern afʿāl, so its pronoun is singular; in 23:21 the feminine plural reflects its collective meaning.
rows.anchor: ذكر سيبويه الأنعام في الأسماء المفردة الواردة على أفعال ولذا رجع الضمير إليه مفردا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates pure milk between dung and blood, separated by a barrier so neither gives it color, taste, or smell; the organ distributes the digested feed into blood, milk, and residue.
rows.anchor: أي يخلق الله اللبن وسيطا بين الفرث والدم يكتفانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An account says feed is cooked in the animal's stomach: residue settles below, milk in the middle, blood above; the liver directs each to veins, udders, or stomach, where the residue descends.
rows.anchor: قيل إذا أكلت البهيمة العلف فاستقر في كرشها وطبخته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This process is evidence for reflection; Shuqayq defines sincerity as separating work from defects as milk is separated from dung and blood.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك عبرة لمن اعتبر وسئل شقيق عن الاخلاص فقال تميز العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The milk is easy to swallow, and it is said no one has ever choked on milk; the first min is partitive, while the second marks the starting point.
rows.anchor: سهل المرور في الحلق ويقال لم يغص أحد باللبن قط ومن الأولى للتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is attached to an omitted 'We give you drink' from date-palm and grape fruits, meaning their juice; the omission is supplied by the preceding verb.
rows.anchor: بمحذوف تقديره ونسقيكم من ثمرات النخيل والأعناب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about making sugar explains the drinking or repeats minhu for emphasis; the pronoun returns to the omitted juice.
rows.anchor: بيان وكشف عن كنه الاسقاء أو تتخذون ومنه من تكرير الظرف للتوكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sukr means wine, named by its verbal noun; alternatively, the verse predates wine's prohibition and is abrogated, or it combines a reproach with a blessing.
rows.anchor: والسكر الخمر سميت بالمصدر من سكر سكرا

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأبو يوسف
rows.claim: They hold that nabīdh from grapes, raisins, or dates boiled until two-thirds evaporate and then fermented remains lawful until it intoxicates; they argue from this verse, a prophetic report, and many reports.
rows.anchor: وهو عصير العنب والزبيب والتمر إذا طبخ حتى يذهب ثلثاه ثم يترك حتى يشتد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good provision includes vinegar, syrup, dates, raisins, and other wholesome products.
rows.anchor: هو الخل والرب والتمر والزبيب وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs in these fruits are evidence for people who reason.
rows.anchor: إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يعقلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God takes people's souls; the most decrepit age is variously set at seventy-five, eighty, or ninety.
rows.anchor: إلى أخسه وأحقره وهو خمس وسبعون سنة أو ثمانون أو تسعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of extreme old age may be that a person forgets what was learned, or ceases to acquire further knowledge.
rows.anchor: لينسى ما يعلم أو لئلا يعلم زيادة علم على علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the wisdom of transforming people from their prime toward decline or from life toward extinction, and can change whatever He wills.
rows.anchor: بحكم التحويل إلى الارذل من الأكمل أو إلى الافناء من الاحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bound hand and hand spread fully illustrate miserliness and extravagance; kull is an accusative verbal noun, and the command is moderation between the two.
rows.anchor: كل نصب على المصدر لاضافته إليه وهذا تمثيل لمنع الشحيح وإعطاء المسرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The squanderer is blameworthy before God, people, and himself when later need brings regret; maḥsūr means depleted and unable to go on, or bareheaded.
rows.anchor: فتصير ملوما عند الله لأن المسرف غير مرضى عنده وعند الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Muslim woman wagered with her Jewish co-wife that Muhammad was more generous than Moses; her daughter asked for his shirt, he gave it and sat naked, missing prayer, whereupon the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقد خاطرت مسلمة ضرتها اليهودية فى أنه يعنى محمدا عليه السلام أجود من موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks for mercy from God's stores, including forgiveness, provision, and safety from enemies.
rows.anchor: رحمة من خزائن رحمتك وهي المغفرة والرزق والامن من الاعداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their affair means their separation from the unbelievers; they ask God to prepare a right course so they become guided, or to make their whole affair rightly guided, or to ease the path to His pleasure.
rows.anchor: الذي نحن عليه من مفارقة الكفار ﴿ رشدا ﴾ حتى نكون بسببه راشدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God placed a curtain over their ears, meaning He caused deep sleep that sounds could not interrupt; the object 'barrier' is omitted.
rows.anchor: أي ضربنا عليها حجابا من النوم يعني أنمناهم إنامة ثقيلة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says 'counted years' means years counted because a large number needs counting; a small number can be known without counting, whereas a counted home indicates few inhabitants.
rows.anchor: أي تعد عددا لكثرتها لأن القليل يعلم مقداره من غير عدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God awakened them; the two groups differed about how long they slept, with the ones saying 'God knows' realizing the duration was long, or the groups may be outsiders debating it.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لنعلم أي الحزبين ﴾ المتخلفين منهم في مدة لبثهم لأنهم لما انتبهوا اختلفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥṣā is a past-tense verb and amad is its adverb or object; together with its subject it fills the two complements of 'we know,' meaning which group best measured or comprehended the duration.
rows.anchor: وأحصى فعل ماض وأمدا ظرف لأحصى أو مفعول به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking aḥṣā as the superlative 'best at counting' is mistaken because forming it from a non-triliteral verb is not analogical.
rows.anchor: ومن قال أحصى أفعل من الاحصاء وهو العد فقد زل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'So that We may know' means making the result known to them, increasing their faith and reflection, and providing a clear sign to unbelievers; alternatively, God actualizes their disagreement already known to Him.
rows.anchor: لأن المراد ما تعلق به العلم من ظهور الأمر لهم ليزدادوا إيمانا واعتبارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account is true; فتية is the plural of fatā. Futuwwa means generosity, refraining from harm and complaint, avoiding forbidden acts, and practicing virtues.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إنهم فتية ﴾ جمع فتى والفتوة بذل الندى وكف الأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another definition says a youth does not claim virtue before acting or praise himself after acting.
rows.anchor: وقيل الفتى من لا يدعي قبل الفعل ولا يزكي نفسه بعد الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God increased their guidance as certainty; they were close associates of Diqyanus, and God placed faith in their hearts.
rows.anchor: ﴿ آمنوا بربهم وزدناهم هدى ﴾ يقينا وكانوا من خواص دقيانوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afraid to disclose faith in a group, they paired off, each pair privately revealing its belief, and then discovered their agreement.
rows.anchor: وخاف بعضهم بعضا وقالوا ليخل اثنان اثنان منا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God strengthened their hearts to endure abandoning their homes and fleeing for faith, and emboldened them to proclaim the truth and profess Islam.
rows.anchor: وقويناها بالصبر على هجران الأوطان والفرار بالدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They stood before the tyrant Diqyanus without fear when he reproached them for abandoning idol worship.
rows.anchor: بين يدي الجبار وهو دقيانوس من غير مبالاة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They proudly declare God alone is Lord of the heavens and earth; calling another god would be excessive injustice and falsehood.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فقالوا ربنا رب السماوات والأرض ﴾ مفتخرين ﴿ لن ندعوا من دونه إلها ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaṭaṭ means excessive injustice and going too far, from a root meaning to be distant.
rows.anchor: قولا ذا شطط وهو الافراط في الظلم والابعاد فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers address one another after firmly resolving to flee with their religion; what they worship is grammatically coordinated to the pronoun, meaning abandon the people and their objects of worship.
rows.anchor: خطاب من بعضهم لبعض حيث صممت عزيمتهم على الفرار بدينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may be connected because the people acknowledged the Creator but associated partners; or disconnected, referring to unbelievers and their idols; alternatively, it is God's parenthetical report that the youths worshipped none but Him.
rows.anchor: استثناء متصل لأنهم كانوا يقرون بالخالق ويشركون معه غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They tell each other to make the cave their refuge; God will spread mercy, meaning provision, and prepare a useful means of ease.
rows.anchor: صيروا إليه واجعلوا الكهف مأواكم ﴿ ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته ﴾ من رزقه

rows.speaker: المدني والشامي
rows.claim: The Madinan and Shami readings have marfiqan.
rows.anchor: مرفقا مدني وشامي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their confidence and strong hope rest on trust in God and clear certainty; alternatively, a prophet of their time told them this.
rows.anchor: ثقة بفضل الله وقوة في رجائهم لتوكلهم عليه ونصوع يقينهم
